expected.summary: Eleven minutes before the anchor the security team (SEC-2304) began applying the WAF ruleset owasp-crs-4.7 at paranoia level 2, with request body inspection, to edge-gateway, one pod every twenty seconds; each edge-gateway pod logged a config.change when it took effect, and edge-gateway's version did not change. Rule 942440 uses a regular expression that backtracks on checkout's JSON request bodies, so on every enforced pod POST /checkout spends about 170 ms in inspection and about 40 percent of checkout requests hit the 250 ms inspection timeout. The WAF fails closed, so edge-gateway answers 503 WAF inspection timeout: rule 942440 exceeded 250ms on request body, request blocked, without forwarding the request. The failures start and stay at edge-gateway itself: web-bff, mobile-bff, checkout and everything behind them are healthy and simply receive fewer checkout requests, and blocked customers are never charged. GET routes carry no body and are unaffected. mobile-bff 2.4.0, rolled out about thirty one minutes before the anchor, is unrelated: it served cleanly for twenty minutes before the ruleset took effect, and the blocked requests never reach it.
contributingFactors: the SEC-2304 WAF ruleset owasp-crs-4.7 applied to edge-gateway with request body inspection and a fail-closed 250 ms timeout
rule 942440's regular expression backtracking on checkout's JSON request bodies

criteria.description: Does the brief place the origin at edge-gateway itself, in the SEC-2304 owasp-crs-4.7 WAF ruleset with request body inspection, whose rule 942440 times out on checkout bodies so the gateway blocks POST /checkout with 503s before forwarding? 5 = the ruleset, the inspection timeout, POST /checkout only and the services behind the gateway healthy. Blaming mobile-bff 2.4.0, checkout or any backend scores at most 2; saying only 'edge-gateway is failing' with no ruleset scores at most 2.

Is it grounded in the WAF inspection timeout errors on edge-gateway spans, the config.change logs on each gateway pod lining up with each pod's first failures, the failures confined to POST /checkout, and checkout traffic dropping behind the gateway with no errors there? Cap at 3 unless it notes that the requests never reach the backends.
Does it avoid blaming mobile-bff 2.4.0, checkout, payment or orders, and avoid calling a GET route affected?
Concise, structured, no filler or speculation.
